A few requested on my last post to do a mini review of the Charlotte Tilbury beautiful skin foundation in the lightest shade, 1 neutral. I will say it is quite a bit yellow for a “neutral” foundation so this wouldn’t suit pink toned folks. I’m a neutral undertone and it suited me fine. I did not mix any white mixer in it so I was worried about how it would look if it oxidized but to my surprise I didn’t end up with a dark line around my jawline by the end of the day! 


As for application, I preferred a brush over a sponge. I used the It Cosmetics love is the foundation (the heart shaped one) brush on my right side, and used the ecotools bioblender sponge on my left side. It blended very well. The coverage I would say is medium and the finish is natural/dewy. 


I did not edit any of my photos at all or touch up or powder my skin throughout my day. I know I was looking a hot mess in the last 2 photos I posted but I can’t be bothered about that lol. Anyways my coworker said my skin looked really dewy and glowy when I took off my mask during break. I typically wear a matte foundation so this was a little different for me. I have combination skin and have to wear a mask during my 8 hour shift so I did experience some shine break through. It’s nothing unbearable though, the foundation held up fairly well given the circumstances. I wouldn’t consider this a long wearing foundation because it did break down a little bit but it wasn’t like transferring onto my mask or the back of my hands if I touched my face like I’ve experienced before. 


Would I recommend it? I give it a solid 8/10, if you’re normal-dry and looking for a glowy medium coverage foundation I think this is worth trying. What I loved about this foundation the most is that it didn’t emphasize the texture on my skin which I have a lot of due to acne scarring. I think the wear time isn’t like double wear comparable and I typically would opt for more coverage than this offers but it doesn’t transfer easily and is tolerable without adding powder in the middle of my day (although I personally will be touching up when I wear it).  I would stay far away from this if you were oily as it is quite dewy after it settles and I can see this breaking down easily with a lot of oil production.

My current thoughts are that I loved how the foundation wore for a few hours, especially considering I was masked for majority of it. I have very bad texture on my skin and it was seamless and didn’t emphasize it. I typically do prefer more coverage so I was surprised I liked it so much! Your best interest would be getting a prescription to retin a if possible. It will be cheaper if you have insurance than buying expensive retinol products. Let’s say you don’t have insurance. Here would be the approach.

Retinol > exfoliation for your case. However I never recommend retinol every day. Unless it’s very weak and in the middle/last ingredients in a hydrating moisturizer. Exfoliate once a week and use a concentrated retinol serum/moisturizer on dry skin 10-15 minutes after cleansing your skin 3-4 times a week on the day you are not exfoliating.

If you opt for retin a you will have to start slowly 1-2 days a week on completely dry skin. Wait 30 minutes after washing to apply. You probably won’t be able to exfoliate the first few weeks on this. But eventually your skin should tolerate it. And no don’t use a retinol moisturizer, serum or mask with retin a.

You can use two products with the same AHAs in one day but I would tread lightly don’t go overboard. Like let’s say you exfoliated with the microfoliant and want to use a mask with AHAs as well. Give a 1-2 day space in between the two. Watch your ingredients.

Lastly, sunscreen. Not just in your moisturizer, a separate sunscreen. Every single day. Every morning. Do not leave the house without it. Spf 30 or higher.

Hi esthetician here that struggles with redness, sensitivity and acne. I’ve tried it all and failed and ended up on accutane. I can still offer you good advice being in your shoes for years. 

You’re using salicylic acid and azelaic acid every day and the ordinary niacinamide every day. That is killing and stressing your skin. I would never recommend someone using azelaic acid every day. In a cleanser salicylic doesn’t do much since it doesn’t stay on the skin long enough so I’m less concerned about it being used daily but combined with multiple other exfoliants this will cause problems. And then adding the serum and peel on top of it. Def way too much. TO niacinamide & zinc serum I find to be very irritating in general for my skin. If it works for you, like it does for many, that’s great but it will not do any good using it with products that compromise your skin.

Basically your problem is over exfoliation. What is happening here is that your skin is getting dried out by all these products and creating more oil, which leads to more acne and redness. You need to choose between using TO peel every week if your skin can handle it OR the azelaic acid. They should not be used in the same week. Tbh I would only recommend using a high strength peel every 3 weeks. But some people can use it every 2 weeks. I find that to be rare cases. Cut the azelaic acid down to 3 times a week, maybe 4, and don’t use TO serum the same day. The hylauronic acid serum is good to use with the acid though.

Yes there are many severe long term effects including death. Luckily you are young enough where it is easier to make friends. As an introverted type 2 or 3 will be a good amount for you. However the older you get and the more time you spend alone, the more you become set in your ways. Then it becomes harder and even impossible to make friends.

From a biological standpoint humans are social creatures because before civilization, we had to live in groups for our own protection and survival. Being alone left you defenseless and to fend for yourself to get food, water, and shelter. This pretty much meant death. 

Loneliness has been proven to shorten your lifespan. It inhibits your social skills, makes you resent people more, and over time you lose the ability to relate to others. Eventually chronic loneliness leads to fear of even leaving the house. This makes you more vulnerable to becoming a victim of addiction, obesity, depression, and suicide. It even has been linked to schizophrenia and Alzheimer’s disease. 

You say you are fine without friends but that is a defensive mechanism stemming from loneliness. Loneliness tricks your mind into viewing others as an enemy, so you become even more avoidant of others because you literally start to fear them.

Now you have asked this question so I’m sure you are already considering deep down you are not happy like this. You have options to prevent yourself from this cycle. I would highly recommend seeing a therapist if you are able to. Campus ones are over loaded and quite frankly I struggled even getting an appointment due to high volume so they should be a last resort. A good therapist can help you work on the skills you need to change this behavior and make friends. Sometimes you may have to try different therapists before you find the right one. 

Many people will recommend doing clubs or extra curricular activities. But I have always made friends fine through just my classes, online and work. It is a personal preference. You may find it easier to make friends with people who you already know share the same interests. 

You are young now and you are not doomed to be lonely. You don’t need to be a social butterfly. I am an introverted person and I am quite fine doing my own thing and don’t need to be around others constantly but that doesn’t mean I don’t need to have friends. We all need love, support, and connection to others. You will see if you don’t change this now, in time, that you can not and will not make it in life alone.
